# Sound It Out

> Sound It Out started as a reading site and has grown into something much larger: free printable worksheets, worksheet makers, books and guided learning paths for reading, writing and math, for children ages 4 to 8 (preschool, kindergarten, first grade and the start of second grade), built around school standards. Free tools show where to start and point to what may be causing the difficulty. 10-day plans teach one difficulty each, with printable pages, a short video for each day and sound tracks for the child ($19, one payment, 30-day money back). Every printable pack and bundle is free to download.

## Start here
- [Find your child’s reading level](https://sounditoutreading.com/#start): a free level finder with a plan for the week
- [My child is behind in reading: where do I start?](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-is-behind-in-reading/): a free finder that points to what may be causing the difficulty. For grade 2.
- [Free 3-minute check: Hearing the sounds in words](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-hear-the-sounds-in-words/): Your child cannot rhyme or say what sound a word starts with. This free 3-minute check shows where the listening stops and what to do next.
- [Free 3-minute check: Knowing the letters](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-doesnt-know-letters/): Your child doesn’t know the letters yet, or knows only some. This free 3-minute check shows which ones, and what to do tonight. For kindergarten.
- [Free 3-minute check: The letter sounds](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-remember-letter-sounds/): Your child does not know the letter sounds or keeps forgetting them. This free 3-minute check shows where to start and what to do tonight.
- [Free 3-minute check: Putting sounds together](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-blend-sounds/): Your child knows the letter sounds but cannot blend them into a word. This free 3-minute check points to the likely reason and what to do tonight. For kindergarten.
- [Free 3-minute check: Consonant blends](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-teach-blends/): Your child reads cat and hop but not stop, frog or jump. This free 3-minute check shows where to start teaching blends, and what to do tonight. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [Free 3-minute check: sh, ch, th and other pairs](https://sounditoutreading.com/which-digraphs-to-teach-first/): Your child reads cat and hop but not ship, chin or ring. This free 3-minute check shows which digraphs to teach first, and what to do tonight. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [Free 3-minute check: Guessing at words](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-guess-words-when-reading/): Your child guesses at words instead of sounding them out. This free 3-minute check shows which guessing habit it is and what to do tonight.
- [Free 3-minute check: Mixing up b and d](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-mix-up-b-and-d/): Your child mixes up b and d. This free 3-minute check shows whether the mix-up is in reading, writing or both, and what to do tonight.
- [Free 3-minute check: Common words that will not stay](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-cant-my-child-remember-sight-words/): Your child learns sight words and forgets them. This free 3-minute check shows where to start and what to do tonight. For kindergarten.
- [Free 3-minute check: Silent e and long vowels](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-cant-read-silent-e-words/): Your child reads cat and hop but not cake, hope or rain. This free 3-minute check shows where the trouble starts and what to do tonight. For grade 1.
- [Free 3-minute check: Vowel teams and bossy r](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-teach-vowel-teams/): Your child reads cake and rain but not play, star or cloud. This free 3-minute check shows where to start teaching vowel teams and bossy r. For grade 2.
- [Free 3-minute check: Long words](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-teach-two-syllable-words/): Your child reads short words but freezes at rabbit or napkin. This free 3-minute check shows where to start teaching two-syllable words. For grade 2.
- [Free 3-minute check: Slow, word-by-word reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/why-does-my-child-read-so-slowly/): Your child reads slowly or sounds out every word. This free 3-minute check shows where the reading sticks and what to do tonight.
- [Free 3-minute check: Reading without taking it in](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-can-read-but-does-not-understand/): Your child can read the words but cannot tell you what they said. This free 3-minute check shows where the meaning gets lost.
- [Free 3-minute check: Spelling](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-can-read-but-cant-spell/): Your child reads simple words but cannot spell them. This free 3-minute check shows where the spelling gets stuck and what to do tonight.
- [Free 3-minute check: Counting and early math](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-help-a-child-struggling-with-math/): Your child struggles with math: counting, numbers or adding. This free 3-minute check shows which step is hard and what to do tonight. For pre-K to kindergarten.
- [Free 3-minute check: Writing a sentence](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-child-cant-write-a-sentence/): Your child writes words but not a sentence: no capital, no spaces, no period. This free 3-minute check shows where to start tonight. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [Free 3-minute check: Handwriting](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-help-my-child-with-handwriting/): Your child’s handwriting is messy or letters face the wrong way. This free 3-minute check shows where the trouble is and what to do tonight.

## Programs and daily sheets
- [The Reading Program](https://sounditoutreading.com/reading-program-for-struggling-readers/): all fifteen reading plans in order, from first sounds to reading on their own, with a short video for every day; one payment. For ages 4 to 8.
- [The One Sheet for Reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/the-one-sheet/): one printed reading sheet a day, made for the child from how the day before went; a monthly plan, cancel any time
- [The One Sheet for Math](https://sounditoutreading.com/the-one-sheet-math/): one printed math sheet a day: counting, adding and taking away; a monthly plan
- [The One Sheet for Grammar](https://sounditoutreading.com/the-one-sheet-grammar/): one printed grammar sheet a day: capital letters, periods, is and are; a monthly plan

## Make a full pack
- [Short A Worksheets for Kindergarten: make a free pack](https://sounditoutreading.com/short-a-worksheets-for-kindergarten/): pick the kinds of short a words pages and print one pack of 20 to 60 pages, with the child's name on the cover and answer keys; kindergarten and 1st grade

## Guides for parents
- [Guides: find the problem that sounds like your child](https://sounditoutreading.com/guides/): every guide and problem page in one place, by what parents see at home. For kindergarten and grade 2.
- [Signs of dyslexia in kids](https://sounditoutreading.com/signs-of-dyslexia-in-kids/): what to look for at each age and how to ask the school for an evaluation; not a test. For pre-K to grade 2.
- [My second grader is behind in reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-help-struggling-reader-2nd-grade/): what behind means, step by step, and where to start. For grade 2.
- [How to pronounce the letter sounds](https://sounditoutreading.com/how-to-pronounce-letter-sounds/): hear every letter sound, said short and clean
- [The Reading Lab](https://sounditoutreading.com/reading-research/): what the research says about teaching reading, with sources

## Free worksheet makers
- [Free worksheet maker](https://sounditoutreading.com/free-worksheet-maker/): every free make-your-own worksheet tool in one place (reading, handwriting, math, grammar). For pre-K to grade 1.

## 10-day plans
- [Ears First](https://sounditoutreading.com/ears-first-10-day-listening-plan/): Cannot tell me the first sound of a word, or cannot rhyme. The goal: on day 10 your child hears the sounds in a short word. They say how it starts, push three sounds together into a word, and pull a word apart into its sounds. For ages 4 to 6.
- [Know Every Letter](https://sounditoutreading.com/know-every-letter-10-day-letter-recognition-plan/): Does not know many letters yet, or knows the big ones but not the small ones. The goal: on day 10 your child names all 26 letters, big and small, even in a typeface never seen in the book. For ages 4 to 6.
- [Eight Sounds That Stay](https://sounditoutreading.com/eight-sounds-that-stay-10-day-plan/): Does not know the letter sounds, or learns them and forgets them. The goal: on day 10 your child says the sound of eight letters, in any order, a day after the last lesson, and uses them to read short words never seen before. For ages 4 to 6.
- [From Sounds to Words](https://sounditoutreading.com/from-sounds-to-words-blending-plan/): Knows the sounds, but cannot put them together into a word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads words they have never seen before. For ages 4 to 7.
- [Stop and Jump](https://sounditoutreading.com/stop-and-jump-consonant-blends-10-day-plan/): Reads short words like cat, but reads stop as top, or stops at frog and jump. The goal: on day 10 your child says every sound in words like stop, jump and frog, and reads blend words never seen before. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Ship and Chip](https://sounditoutreading.com/ship-and-chip-digraphs-10-day-plan/): Reads short words like cat, but says ship as s-h-i-p, or stops at chin, this and ring. The goal: on day 10 your child spots two letters that make one sound, and reads words like ship, chin, this and ring never seen before. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Look at Every Letter](https://sounditoutreading.com/look-at-every-letter-10-day-plan/): Guesses words from the first letter or the picture, or “reads” books from memory. The goal: on day 10 your child looks at every letter before saying a word, and reads words and sentences never seen before, with no picture to help. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Tell b from d](https://sounditoutreading.com/tell-b-from-d-10-day-plan/): Mixes up b and d. The goal: on day 10 your child tells b from d, in letters, in words never seen before, and in their own writing. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Words That Stick](https://sounditoutreading.com/words-that-stick-sight-words-10-day-plan/): Cannot remember common words like the, said and was. The goal: on day 10 your child reads 16 of the most common words, on their own and inside sentences never seen before. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Cap to Cape](https://sounditoutreading.com/cap-to-cape-silent-e-10-day-plan/): Reads short words like cat, but gets stuck on cake, rain and boat. The goal: on day 10 your child looks to the end of a word for a silent e, and reads words like cake, kite and hope never seen before. For ages 5 to 8.
- [Stars and Clouds](https://sounditoutreading.com/stars-and-clouds-vowel-teams-10-day-plan/): Reads cake, rain and boat, but stops at play, star, bird and cloud. The goal: on day 10 your child finds the vowel team or the bossy r, and reads words like play, star, bird and cloud never seen before. For ages 6 to 8.
- [Rabbit and Sunset](https://sounditoutreading.com/rabbit-and-sunset-two-syllable-words-10-day-plan/): Reads short words like ship and frog, but guesses or freezes at rabbit, napkin or jumping. The goal: on day 10 your child splits a long word into its beats, and reads words like rabbit, sunset and jumping never seen before. For ages 6 to 8.
- [Smooth Reading](https://sounditoutreading.com/smooth-reading-10-day-plan/): Reads slowly, one word at a time, or sounds out every word. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short sentence they have never seen, smoothly, the way they would say it. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Read It, See It](https://sounditoutreading.com/read-it-see-it-10-day-plan/): Reads the words but cannot tell me what it said. The goal: on day 10 your child reads a short story they have never seen, tells you what happened, and draws it. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Hear It, Write It](https://sounditoutreading.com/hear-it-write-it-10-day-spelling-plan/): Can read simple words but cannot spell them. The goal: on day 10 your child writes short words they have never practiced, every sound in the right order, and reads each one back to check it. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Count It Up](https://sounditoutreading.com/count-it-up-10-day-math-plan/): Counts one thing twice, or cannot add two small groups yet. The goal: on day 10 your child counts a group by touching each thing once, knows which number is more, and adds two small groups within 10. For ages 4 to 7.
- [My First Sentences](https://sounditoutreading.com/my-first-sentences-10-day-sentence-writing-plan/): Can write some words, but not a sentence: no capital, no spaces, no period. The goal: on day 10 your child writes a sentence they have never written, with a capital, spaces and a period, and reads it back. For ages 5 to 7.
- [Start at the Top](https://sounditoutreading.com/start-at-the-top-10-day-handwriting-plan/): Letters are messy, start in the wrong place or face the wrong way. The goal: on day 10 your child starts every small letter in the right place, sits it on the line, and writes new words that you can read. For ages 5 to 7.

## Free
- [All free worksheets](https://sounditoutreading.com/free-printable-worksheets/): free sample pages from every pack, plus a free reading app. For pre-K to kindergarten.
- [Free reading app](https://sounditoutreading.com/app/): reading games in the browser where every word can be sounded out
- [What Works in Teaching Reading? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-what-works-in-teaching-reading/): research summary. Two large U.S. reviews point the same way. Here is what they found and how strong the evidence is. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Phonics Work? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-does-phonics-work/): research summary. Eighteen studies met the standards of a U.S. review. Here is what they showed, and what they did not test. Every finding names its source.
- [Hearing Sounds in Words: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-hearing-the-sounds-in-words/): research summary. Seventeen studies met the standards of a U.S. review, and all seventeen found positive effects. Every finding names its source.
- [Mixing Up b and d: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-mixing-up-b-and-d/): research summary. An expert panel says it is common in the early grades, and sets out one letter at a time as the way through. Every finding names its source.
- [Blending Sounds Into Words: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-blending-sounds-into-words/): research summary. An expert panel names this exact problem and sets out what to teach. Every finding names its source.
- [Letter Names or Letter Sounds First? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-letter-names-or-letter-sounds/): research summary. The guide teaches each letter with its sound, a few at a time. Every finding names its source.
- [Sight Words: Memorize or Sound Out? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-sight-words-memorize-or-sound-out/): research summary. Sound out the regular ones. Teach the irregular ones as whole words. Every finding names its source.
- [Guessing Words From Pictures: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-guessing-words-from-pictures/): research summary. A U.S. expert panel discourages guessing, and says why. Every finding names its source.
- [Slow, Word-by-Word Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-slow-reading-and-fluency/): research summary. Reading aloud again and again, with feedback, has the best support. Every finding names its source.
- [Reads the Words but Does Not Understand: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-comprehension/): research summary. Sounding out is needed but is not enough. Here is what the panel recommends. Every finding names its source.
- [Can Read but Cannot Spell: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-teaching-spelling/): research summary. Breaking a word into its sounds helps children spell, the panel found. Every finding names its source.
- [Handwriting Practice: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-handwriting-practice/): research summary. Short practice, letters formed the same way each time, then real writing. Every finding names its source.
- [Reading Aloud to Your Child: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-aloud-to-children/): research summary. It builds spoken language and knowledge of print. It is not the same as teaching how letters stand for sounds. Every finding names its source.
- [Talking, Vocabulary and Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-vocabulary-and-talking/): research summary. The guide says the language of books usually has to be taught. The evidence is rated minimal. Every finding names its source.
- [Decodable Books for Beginners: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-decodable-books/): research summary. A good case for decodable books at the very start. Not forever. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Children Learn to Read Naturally? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-do-children-learn-to-read-naturally/): research summary. A major review says the idea that letters stand for sounds has to be taught to most children. Every finding names its source.
- [Dyslexia: Early Signs and What Helps, From Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-dyslexia-early-signs/): research summary. Two research reviews on the signs, the risk factors and the teaching that has support. Every finding names its source.
- [How Often Should a Child Practice Reading? Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-how-often-to-practice-reading/): research summary. Studies used short, regular sessions. A direct test of short against long was not found. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Rhyming Matter for Reading? What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-does-rhyming-matter/): research summary. Rhyme is an easier first step. The teaching that helped reading most worked on single sounds. Every finding names its source.
- [Reading Longer Words: What the Research Guide Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-longer-words/): research summary. The guide gives a routine: find the parts you know, say them, say them fast, check. Every finding names its source.
- [An Older Child Still Learning to Read: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-older-child-still-a-beginner/): research summary. Phonics still helped older struggling readers. So did reading aloud again and again. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Reading Tutoring Help? What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-tutoring/): research summary. Extra teaching in small groups has strong support for sounding out words. Every finding names its source.
- [Sound Games With or Without Letters? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-sound-games-with-letters/): research summary. Sound work done with letters had bigger effects on reading. Every finding names its source.
- [What Parents Can Do at Home: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-what-parents-can-do-at-home/): research summary. In a review of 14 studies, parents teaching specific skills had the largest effect. Every finding names its source.
- [Do Reading Apps Help Young Children? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-reading-apps/): research summary. A positive average effect, with large differences from app to app. Every finding names its source.
- [Learning to Read in a Second Language: The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-english-as-a-second-language/): research summary. The guide reports English learners learning to read at the same rate in kindergarten to grade 2. Every finding names its source.
- [When to Worry About Reading: What the Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-when-to-worry-about-reading/): research summary. The sources name risk signs and school screening. None gives an age to worry. Every finding names its source.
- [Does Being Read To Predict Reading? The Research](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-being-read-to-and-later-reading/): research summary. Shared reading helps language. Its effect on reading skills is less sure. Every finding names its source.
- [Early Signs of a Future Reader: What Research Says](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-early-predictors-of-reading/): research summary. Knowing letters and hearing the sounds in words are among six early skills with the strongest links. Every finding names its source.
- [Forgetting Letter Sounds: What the Research Guides Say](https://sounditoutreading.com/research-remembering-letter-sounds/): research summary. The guides do not explain the forgetting. They do set out what to do. Every finding names its source.

- [Free Phonics Games for Kindergarten](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-free-phonics-games-for-kindergarten/): Free phonics games for kindergarten that build real reading: listening, blending, word building and sentence games, with tips to make each one count.
- [How to Find Your Child’s Reading Level](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-find-your-childs-reading-level/): How to find your child’s reading level at home: check each reading step in order, listen to your child read a short page, and choose books that fit.
- [How to Help a Struggling Reader at Home](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-help-a-struggling-reader-at-home/): How to help a struggling reader at home: find the step that is hard, teach it in a few minutes a day, read together, and work with the school on support. For grade 2 to grade 3.
- [How to Teach Digraphs: sh, ch and th](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-digraphs/): How to teach digraphs like sh, ch and th: show two letters making one sound, practice with pictures and word lists, and read and spell digraph words. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [How to Teach Nouns to Kids: Simple Steps](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-nouns/): How to teach nouns to kids: naming words for people, places, animals and things, sorting games, plurals, and how nouns fit into simple sentences. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [How to Teach Number Bonds to Kindergarten](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-number-bonds-to-kindergarten/): How to teach number bonds to kindergarten children: split numbers into parts with real objects, use ten frames and bond pictures, and learn bonds to 10.
- [How to Teach Place Value to Kids](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-place-value/): How to teach place value to kids: bundle ten ones into a ten, build numbers with tens and ones, use place value charts, and read two-digit numbers. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [How to Teach Silent E: A Simple Guide](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-silent-e/): How to teach silent e at home: show how the e changes cap to cape, practice word pairs, read and spell silent e words, and know when your child is ready. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [How to Teach Subtraction to Kindergarten](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-how-to-teach-subtraction-to-kindergarten/): How to teach subtraction to kindergarten children: take away with real objects, act out short stories, count back on a number line, and link it to adding.

- [Why Is My Child Writing Letters Backwards?](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-why-is-my-child-writing-letters-backwards/): Why is my child writing letters backwards? Reversals like b and d are common up to about age 7. What causes them, what helps, and when to ask for help.
- [My Child Can Read Words but Not Sentences: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-can-read-words-but-not-sentences/): My child can read words but not sentences: why single words are easier, and the steps that build smooth, meaningful sentence reading at home. For kindergarten to grade 1.
- [My Child Mixes Up B and D: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-mixes-up-b-and-d/): My child mixes up b and d: why it is common at five and six, the steps to teach each letter on its own, and when to talk to the teacher about it.
- [My Child Confuses Words Like Was and Saw: What to Do](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-my-child-confuses-words-like-was-and-saw/): My child confuses words like was and saw: why look-alike words get mixed up, and steps that teach letter-by-letter checking instead of guessing.
- [My Child Can’t Hear the First Sound in a Word](https://sounditoutreading.com/guide-child-cannot-hear-first-sound-in-word/): Why your child can’t hear the first sound in a word yet, and short daily listening games that build this early skill before letters come back in.
